overview.executive_summary: Today’s verified candidates highlight actively exploited vulnerabilities, artificial intelligence-assisted cyberattacks, major data exposure, and important security-support deadlines. Organizations should prioritize urgent patching, review exposed systems and third-party access, and track emerging use of AI-enabled attack tools.

sections.heading: Windows 11 23H2 support deadline
sections.what_happened: Microsoft reminded customers that Enterprise, Education, and IoT Enterprise editions of Windows 11 23H2 will stop receiving security updates next month.
sections.why_it_matters: Unsupported systems will no longer receive security updates.
sections.recommended_attention: Identify affected systems and plan updates before support ends.

sections.heading: Nippon Columbia malware incident
sections.what_happened: Daiichi Kosho disclosed that a malware infection at contractor Nippon Columbia exposed more than 8.7 million customer and employee records.
sections.why_it_matters: The incident affects a large volume of customer and employee information and highlights third-party risk.
sections.recommended_attention: Review contractor access, incident impact, and exposure of organizational records.

sections.heading: Arrest linked to alleged ShinyHunters activity
sections.what_happened: Canadian cybersecurity executive Edward Dubrovsky was arrested in Pennsylvania in connection with alleged extortion activity linked by multiple reports to an FBI crackdown on ShinyHunters.
sections.why_it_matters: The case reflects continuing legal action connected to alleged cyber extortion activity.
sections.recommended_attention: Monitor verified developments and assess exposure to related extortion tactics.

sections.heading: AI agents used against South Korean banks
sections.what_happened: A Chinese hacker used the ARTEX AI penetration testing suite and Claude agents in cyberattacks that affected South Korea’s financial sector.
sections.why_it_matters: The activity shows offensive security tools and AI agents being used together in attacks against financial institutions.
sections.recommended_attention: Review controls around AI-enabled activity and strengthen monitoring of banking environments.

sections.heading: SonicWall SMA 1000 exploitation
sections.what_happened: Threat actors exploited a critical SonicWall Secure Mobile Access 1000 flaw within days of public disclosure. The flaw is CVE-2026-102255, with a CVSS score of 10.0, and involves pre-authenticated server-side request forgery.
sections.why_it_matters: The vulnerability is critical, remotely exploitable, and already being targeted in 135 exploitation attempts after patching information became available.
sections.recommended_attention: Prioritize patching and inspect SonicWall SMA 1000 devices for exploitation.

sections.heading: Bricksforge WordPress vulnerability
sections.what_happened: Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-85097, a CVSS 10.0 flaw in the Bricksforge WordPress plugin that allows unauthenticated attackers to upload and execute arbitrary PHP code, enabling remote code execution.
sections.why_it_matters: Unauthenticated remote code execution can give attackers control of vulnerable WordPress websites.
sections.recommended_attention: Patch or disable affected installations and check for unauthorized code or changes.

sections.heading: CyberXero campaign targeting Ukraine
sections.what_happened: Researchers described an artificial intelligence-augmented campaign targeting WordPress sites, e-commerce platforms, and critical infrastructure entities in Ukraine. The campaign used Cobalt Strike with an orchestration layer powered by Anthropic’s Claude Code and stole more than 628,000 Ukrainian records.
sections.why_it_matters: The campaign combines commodity offensive tools with AI orchestration and has affected multiple types of important organizations.
sections.recommended_attention: Review initial-access defenses, Cobalt Strike detections, and AI-assisted attack indicators.

sections.heading: P7 DarkSword iOS exploit kit
sections.what_happened: Researchers disclosed P7 DarkSword, a previously unseen DarkSword iOS exploit-kit variant with a smaller on-device footprint, keychain and cryptocurrency-wallet theft, and two-way command-and-control communication.
sections.why_it_matters: The variant expands the types of sensitive data and control available to attackers while reducing its device footprint.
sections.recommended_attention: Review mobile threat defenses and protect keychain and cryptocurrency-wallet data.

sections.heading: AITEM attack-surface management launch
sections.what_happened: Criminal IP introduced AITEM, an artificial intelligence-powered approach intended to connect exposure discovery with investigation, risk prioritization, and response.
sections.why_it_matters: The offering addresses the gap between finding exposed assets and acting on associated threats.
sections.recommended_attention: Evaluate whether exposure management processes connect discovery with prioritization and response.

stories.title: Microsoft: Windows 11 23H2 reaches end of support in 30 days
stories.summary: Microsoft has reminded customers that Windows 11 23H2 Enterprise, Education, and IoT Enterprise editions will stop receiving security updates next month.
stories.why_it_matters: Organizations have a limited window to update affected systems before security coverage ends.

stories.title: Nippon Columbia malware incident exposes 8.6 million karaoke fan records
stories.summary: Daiichi Kosho disclosed that a malware infection at contractor Nippon Columbia exposed more than 8.7 million customer and employee records.
stories.why_it_matters: The scale of the exposure and the contractor connection make third-party security and data-protection reviews important.

stories.title: Cyber exec arrested in case allegedly tied to ShinyHunters hackers
stories.summary: Canadian cybersecurity executive Edward Dubrovsky was arrested in Pennsylvania in connection with alleged extortion activity that multiple reports linked to an FBI crackdown on ShinyHunters.
stories.why_it_matters: The arrest is a consequential development in alleged cyber-extortion activity and related law-enforcement action.

stories.title: ARTEX AI, Claude agents used in cyberattacks on South Korean banks
stories.summary: A Chinese hacker used the ARTEX AI penetration testing suite and Claude agents in cyberattacks that shook South Korea’s financial sector.
stories.why_it_matters: The activity demonstrates how AI agents and penetration-testing tools can be combined against financial targets.

stories.title: Criminal IP Introduces AITEM as the Next Evolution of Attack Surface Management
stories.summary: Criminal IP introduced AITEM, an AI-powered approach that connects exposure discovery with investigation, risk prioritization, and response.
stories.why_it_matters: Connecting asset discovery to investigation and response may help organizations act more quickly on exposed systems.

stories.title: Critical SonicWall SMA 1000 Flaw Targeted in 135 Exploitation Attempts After Patch
stories.summary: Threat actors have exploited CVE-2026-102255, a CVSS 10.0 pre-authenticated server-side request forgery flaw in SonicWall Secure Mobile Access 1000 appliances, within days of public disclosure. Researchers observed 135 exploitation attempts.
stories.why_it_matters: Active exploitation of a maximum-severity flaw in remote-access appliances creates an urgent exposure for affected organizations.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit CVSS 10.0 Bricksforge WordPress Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated RCE
stories.summary: Attackers are exploiting CVE-2026-85097, a CVSS 10.0 Bricksforge WordPress plugin flaw that permits unauthenticated attackers to upload and execute arbitrary PHP code, resulting in remote code execution.
stories.why_it_matters: Unauthenticated code execution can enable attackers to take control of vulnerable WordPress websites.

stories.title: CyberXero Uses Claude Code in Campaign That Stole Over 628,000 Ukrainian Records
stories.summary: Researchers disclosed an artificial intelligence-augmented campaign targeting WordPress sites, e-commerce platforms, and critical infrastructure entities in Ukraine. The campaign combined Cobalt Strike with an orchestration layer powered by Anthropic’s Claude Code and stole more than 628,000 Ukrainian records.
stories.why_it_matters: The campaign shows AI orchestration being integrated with established offensive tools across several high-impact target types.

stories.title: P7 DarkSword iOS Exploit Kit Adds Crypto Wallet Data Theft and Remote Commands
stories.summary: Researchers disclosed P7 DarkSword, a previously unseen DarkSword iOS exploit-kit variant that reduces its on-device footprint, adds keychain and cryptocurrency-wallet theft, and supports two-way command-and-control communication.
stories.why_it_matters: The variant combines stealthier device activity with theft of highly sensitive credentials and financial data.

tts.text: Here’s today’s cybersecurity briefing. Microsoft says Windows 11 version 23H2 Enterprise, Education, and Internet of Things Enterprise editions will stop receiving security updates next month, so affected systems need an upgrade plan. A malware infection at contractor Nippon Columbia exposed more than 8.7 million customer and employee records, underscoring the importance of third-party security reviews. Two major attack trends stand out: artificial intelligence-assisted operations. South Korean banks were targeted using the ARTEX AI penetration-testing suite and Claude agents, while a campaign called CyberXero combined Cobalt Strike with Claude Code and stole more than 628,000 Ukrainian records. Defenders also face urgent active exploitation. A critical SonicWall Secure Mobile Access flaw, with a Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures identifier and a CVSS score of 10.0, saw 135 exploitation attempts. A maximum-severity Bricksforge WordPress flaw is also being exploited to achieve remote code execution. Finally, researchers reported a new DarkSword iOS variant that steals keychain and cryptocurrency-wallet data and adds two-way command-and-control. Prioritize patching, review third-party exposure, and strengthen monitoring for AI-assisted attacks.
